question.text: Vindhya Event-Driven Fund (Cat III) invests 80% in listed mid-cap equities across FMCG, IT, and Pharma and 20% in unlisted BFSI names. Using the composite approach illustrated in Example 8.7 (Fund Y), which of the following is the MOST appropriate benchmark construction?

answer.text: Nifty 50 TRI for 100% of the portfolio
A composite: 75% sectoral (NIFTY FMCG/IT/Pharma/Financial Services weighted) + 25% mid-cap benchmark (Nifty Midcap 150 or S&P BSE Midcap)
NIFTY Next 50 alone, because it represents the second tier of large-caps
A fixed 10 percent p.a. hurdle rate, since all Cat III AIFs use absolute-return benchmarks

explanation.text: The Logic: Example 8.7 (Fund Y) applies a composite benchmark of 75% sectoral plus 25% mid-cap to a fund whose portfolio combines thematic sector exposures with a mid-cap tilt. Vindhya's 80% mid-cap sectoral plus 20% unlisted profile follows the same composite logic — sectoral leg for the thematic concentration, mid-cap leg for the cap-size tilt. The Trap: Option A uses Nifty 50 — the wrong cap segment (large-cap, not mid). Option C uses NIFTY Next 50 — still large-cap. Option D wrongly assumes every Cat III uses a fixed-rate benchmark; per Section 8.8 that applies only to absolute-return strategies, not thematic long books. Note: The 75% sectoral + 25% mid-cap weights come straight from Example 8.7's Fund Y composite benchmark.
